issues.description: The template defines the arbitrary-n QFT method with a leading underscore name (_qft_circuit_n_qubits) while the solution implements it as a public method qft_circuit_n_qubits. This visibility/name mismatch between template and solution (and the problem statement referring to the QFT for arbitrary qubits) can confuse students about which method to implement and may cause automated tests or example code to call a different method name than what students edit.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name/signature consistent across template and solution. Rename the template method _qft_circuit_n_qubits to qft_circuit_n_qubits (remove the leading underscore) so students implement the same public API shown in the solution, or alternatively change the solution and problem text to use the underscored name. Ensure the inverse method name matches similarly.

issues.description: The template defines the QFT entrypoint with a leading underscore (_qft_circuit_n_qubits) while the solution implements and exposes the method as qft_circuit_n_qubits. Problem tasks (Exercise 7) and test identifiers refer to the public QFT routine for n qubits. This mismatch between the template's internal-looking name and the solution/tests public name creates an API/identifier inconsistency that will confuse students about which method to implement and may cause automated tests to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's public API match the expected name used in the solution/tests: rename the template method _qft_circuit_n_qubits to qft_circuit_n_qubits (or add a qft_circuit_n_qubits wrapper that calls the underscored implementation). Ensure the inverse method name remains qft_circuit_n_qubits_inverse to keep the API consistent.
